earlier intermediate-point strategy was useful but also narrowed its scope. m178 at 1/1 and 2/1 stayed compact while its 50/1 point was very delayed, and m164 became strongly delayed only toward 50/1; these support scaffold-specific curvature rather than a universal correction. m92 and m78 intermediate points were close enough to support local response modeling. The compact m80 points contrasted with delayed m75 and m78 behavior, strengthening the arrangement-specific ester hypothesis. Nitrogen feedback was stronger than expected: m66, m90, m159, m141, m161, and m202 show distinct basic or acceptor-dependent regimes, while amino-ester rows remain comparatively compact. Donor-rich rows m119, m120, m205, m206, and m207 also showed large completion tails and amount-dependent onset, so this batch adds matched loading contrasts alongside new strong-side and intermediate points.","batch_rationale":"The batch repairs the largest observed failure regions while retaining broad coverage of ordinary and delayed rows. It uses local response curves for m164, m178, m199, m92, m114, m159, m90, m211, m212, m202, m161, m141, m207, m206, and m205; matched amount contrasts test whether their large V2 tails and onset shifts are structural or loading-driven. The fused-ring points m181 and m182 probe geometry-specific endpoint behavior, while m80 is a compact malonate control against the delayed carbonyl families and m78 supplies an arrangement-specific ester curve. Strong-side anchors and intermediate ratios should improve interpolation across condition space, and loading contrasts should help the retrained QGeoGNN separate amount effects from solvent-strength effects. The mixture covers heteroatom, donor, aromatic acceptor, fused-ring, ester, and compact control rows so that improvements can transfer across the Row-distribution rather than fitting only one high-error scaffold."}
